purpose: Separate audience-evidence and audience-hypothesis graph. It avoids treating brand intent, testimonials, or social imagery as validated customer segmentation.

nodes.label: Hellobiotic public audience evidence
nodes.summary: A bounded map of public audience signals, not a CRM, media-audience export, or validated ICP.

nodes.label: All-bodies brand intent
nodes.summary: The founder story says the deodorant was intended to work across age, body type, and sex. This is brand intent, not evidence of who purchases or responds best.

nodes.label: Natural-deodorant switch context
nodes.summary: The FAQ directly addresses people switching from standard antiperspirants to a nature-based deodorant, including a possible adjustment period. It evidences a framed transition context, not segment size.

nodes.label: Whole-body care framing
nodes.summary: The storefront presents whole-body and unisex positioning. It signals intended relevance across use contexts without proving actual usage patterns.

nodes.label: Warm-weather, body-and-ritual social framing
nodes.summary: The public Instagram grid visibly uses sun, water, bodies, towels, citrus, heat, and product-in-hand imagery. This indicates brand expression, not follower demographics or conversion intent.

nodes.label: Public testimonial layer
nodes.summary: The storefront displays testimonial statements. They may surface language and concerns, but they are not representative customer research or outcome proof.

nodes.label: Understand deodorant versus antiperspirant
nodes.summary: The FAQ devotes explanatory content to this distinction, showing that the brand considers it relevant to its public education journey; it does not prove a customer knowledge deficit.

nodes.label: Understand microbiome-friendly positioning
nodes.summary: The site contains dedicated microbiome explanation and product education. This is a documented education topic, not a validated customer job-to-be-done.

nodes.label: Natural-deodorant transition explorer
nodes.summary: Working hypothesis: a person evaluating a switch from conventional antiperspirant may need odor education and transition expectations. Do not target or size this group without first-party or independent research.

nodes.label: Sunlit body-care ritual seeker
nodes.summary: Working hypothesis: the seasonal, tactile visual system could resonate with people who treat deodorant as body care rather than a purely functional task. No behavioral or demographic proof is available.

nodes.label: Inclusive whole-body-care explorer
nodes.summary: Working hypothesis: the all-bodies and whole-body framing may invite a broad, non-gendered audience. It must not be converted into an assumed demographic or persona.

nodes.label: No first-party behavioral, conversion, retention, or survey data
nodes.summary: The bounded public corpus has no analytics, CRM, purchase cohorts, ad-platform results, interviews, or surveys. It cannot establish audience size, value, conversion, or retention.

nodes.label: No validated demographics, geography, or media-targeting criteria
nodes.summary: Public brand language and visible social content do not justify a demographic, geographic, or interest-targeting recommendation.
